cards.fix_question: A learner's model shows replication like this: the two original strands stay together, and a whole new double helix is built next to them from new pieces. Discuss whether this model shows semi-conservative replication correctly and suggest how to fix it.
cards.fix_answer:
The model is wrong: it keeps the original molecule whole and builds a completely new molecule, which is not semi-conservative.
Fix: separate the two original strands by breaking the 'hydrogen bonds'; use each as a template; add complementary nucleotide pieces to each and join them into a backbone. Result: two molecules, each with one original and one new strand.

cards.fix_question: State four features of the genetic code.
cards.fix_answer:
Any four of:
1. Triplet code: three bases code for one amino acid.
2. Non-overlapping: read in separate groups of three.
3. Universal: the same triplets code for the same amino acids in almost all organisms.
4. Degenerate: most amino acids have more than one triplet.
5. Has start and stop triplets.

cards.fix_question: Name the three types of gene mutation and outline how each may affect the polypeptide.
cards.fix_answer:
Substitution: one base is swapped for another. Only one codon changes, so at most one amino acid changes (or none, as the code is degenerate); if the new codon is a stop codon the polypeptide is shortened.
Insertion: an extra base is added. The codons after it are read in a different grouping (frameshift), so many amino acids may change.
Deletion: a base is removed. This also causes a frameshift, so many amino acids may change.
